title: The Effect of Perceived Similarity and Accuracy in Ideal Partner Preferences on Relationship Satisfaction
abstract: ABSTRACT How partners perceive one another may be important for relationship satisfaction, particularly when those perceptions concern ideal partner preferences. The present study tested whether perceived similarity (alignment between one's own ideals and one's perceptions of a partner's ideals) and accuracy (alignment between one's perceptions of a partner's ideals and a partner's reported ideals) are associated with relationship satisfaction. A sample of 136 mixed‐gender couples ( N = 272), dating for an average of 16 months, reported their own ideals, their perceptions of their partner's ideals, and their relationship satisfaction. Actor‐Partner Interdependence Models (APIMs) revealed that individuals' perceived similarity predicted their own, and their partner's, relationship satisfaction. By contrast, accuracy did not predict relationship satisfaction, although exploratory analyses showed that other aspects of accuracy (e.g., the degree to which one perceives themselves as accurate about their partner) were associated with greater satisfaction. Taken together, these findings suggest that subjective beliefs about similarity and accuracy might be more strongly linked to relationship satisfaction than objective correspondence.
